messages:
sita: Heads-up — I found a group of ephemeral-embedding records with TTL set to 90d instead of the expected 7d after last night's infra migration. Looks like a lifecycle policy got applied to the snapshots bucket. :eyes:
jonathan: ugh. which bucket/pattern? can you paste the object key(s)?
sita: s3://redwood-embeddings/prod/eph/2026/03/21/embedding-97a3...gz and a bunch in the same prefix. only affects the EU region cluster.
maria: deploy-bot reported the storage lifecycle change in the migration PR: https://git.internal/r/migrations/632. PR comment shows `apply-lifecycle: true` but we assumed default 7d.
kevin: if TTL was longer the DSAR delete flow might not have seen them as expired — legal might flag this as a retention exception. @liz-legal can you advise on risk/next steps?
liz-legal: If ephemeral embeddings were retained beyond their declared TTL we need to log an incident and prepare a notification on affected subjects if it's material. Need numbers: how many users, how long extended for, and whether data was accessible to anyone outside intended ephemeral process.
sita: rough numbers: ~14k objects, EU-only, earliest misapplied change 2026-03-20 22:13 UTC, so ~48 hours exposure. Not aware of any external access.
jonathan: from infra POV we should 1) ensure lifecycle corrected, 2) run the DSAR erasure pipeline against the affected prefixes, 3) create a retention-exception record if legal requests it.
maria: two technical concerns: 1) the erasure job needs a service account with DeleteObject + kms:Decrypt for snapshots encrypted with customer keystores; 2) audit logs currently show the lifecycle transition but not object-level deletes from the erasure pipeline — we must ensure audit events are emitted and stored for compliance.
kevin: for (1) I can create a timebound role `roles/dsar_erasure_runner` scoped to that bucket and only active for 24h. policy sketch:
```
principals: serviceAccount:dsar-erasure@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
permissions:
  - storage.objects.delete
  - storage.objects.get
  - kms.decrypt
resource: projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu/keyRings/emb-keys/cryptoKeys/prod
condition: request.time < "2026-03-23T02:00:00Z"
```
kevin: open Q: does `kms.decrypt` need to be on the key or the key ring for our cloud provider? (I'm on GCP but some customers use external KMS).
jonathan: kms permission usually on the key resource itself. For external HSMs we have to use the keystore proxy token — sec team, any gotchas?
sec-bot: notice: keystore-rotation job completed 2026-03-19 04:12 UTC. No failed operations reported.
sec-bot: alert: object-delete-audit-write missing for erasure-runner role on sample run at 4800002240 — action required.
kevin: ok we need to add logging permission: `storage.objects.get` + `logging.logEntries.create` or IAM role that writes audit events. How do we guarantee logs are immutable for retention evidence?
maria: we ship logs to a scrubbed audit log bucket with retention and WORM enabled. The erasure-runner must be allowed to write an event to the audit queue; better: the erasure job should publish an explicit signed receipt per object to the audit service (so we don't rely on cloud provider object delete logs alone).
liz-legal: receipts per object are ideal for DSAR evidence. If we can produce a canonical list with signed timestamps and the service account identity that performed the deletion, that will satisfy regulators.
sita: plan proposal: (A) revert lifecycle to 7d and confirm no other prefixes affected, (B) provision timebound `dsar_erasure` role with kms:decrypt on the specific key and logging write, (C) run erasure pipeline that emits signed receipts to audit service, (D) capture counts and draft retention-exception record for legal review.
jonathan: also add a postmortem to cover why migration PR defaulted to apply-lifecycle true. small blunder but we need guardrails (unit test or lint).
kevin: I'll draft the IAM role and run a dry run against a staging prefix. posting rough policy now in infra-ops.
maria: I'll instrument the erasure job to emit receipts and ensure they go to the immutable audit bucket.
liz-legal: I'll prepare a retention-exception template and confirm notification threshold. For now label this Priority: P2 until we quantify affected subjects.
sita: thanks — I'll start the object inventory and share numbers in this thread in ~30m. :thumbsup:
